scenario_name: Order status followed by unsupported address change
judge_summary: The assistant handled the order inquiry smoothly, giving precise status details and transparently stating system limitations around changing the address or adding notes. It maintained consistent context, used a clear and courteous tone, and offered a reasonable workaround via Swiss Post, though it could have been slightly more helpful by proactively suggesting escalation to human customer support for pre-shipment address changes.

bot: Hello—what can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Hi, I want to check the status and ETA of my Galaxy Watch order, please.
bot: Right, let me check on that order.

Your **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** order (**ORD-20260628-001**, placed **June 28, 2026**) is currently **being prepared for shipment at the distribution center** (no tracking number yet—it's assigned once it ships). The current estimates are **ship: July 1, 2026** and **delivery: July 3–5, 2026** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)** to **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich**.

transcript.user: Thanks. Can you redirect the delivery to a different address instead of Bahnhofstrasse 42?
bot:
I can look into the options for that. At the moment, I don’t have a tool here that can change or redirect the shipping address on an existing order.

If you tell me the **new address** and whether you’re able to receive **Swiss Post deliveries at either address**, I can advise the best next step (for example, whether to contact Swiss Post directly once tracking is issued).

transcript.user: The new address would be: Morgartenstrasse 15, 8004 Zürich. And yes, I can receive Swiss Post deliveries there too. Can you just update it in the system anyway, even if the label can’t be changed yet?
bot: Okay, one moment. I’ll check what details are available for that order.

transcript.user: Sure, thanks. Please let me know if you’re able to update anything on your side for that address change.
bot: Right, let me pull up that order again.

For **ORD-20260628-001**, the shipping address on file still shows **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich**, and I don’t have a way in this chat to update an order’s delivery address in our system.

Once the watch ships and **tracking becomes available**, you can usually request a **Swiss Post reroute/hold** to **Morgartenstrasse 15, 8004 Zürich** directly with Swiss Post using that tracking number.

transcript.user: Okay, understood. Can you still add a note or comment on the order in your system with the new address, even if it doesn’t change the shipping label?
bot:
I’ll take a quick look at what I can do from here.  

I don’t have a tool available in this chat to **add notes/comments to an order** (or to update the address) in our system. The best workaround is to **reroute with Swiss Post once tracking is issued**, using the tracking number when it appears.

transcript.user: Got it. Just to confirm, nothing at all was changed on my order, and the shipping address is still Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich, correct?
bot:
Correct — nothing has been changed on **ORD-20260628-001** from my side, and the shipping address still shows **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich**.

It’s still **OPEN / being prepared for shipment**, and **tracking isn’t available yet** (it will be assigned once it ships).

transcript.user: Perfect, thanks for confirming—that’s all I needed.
bot: Can I help you with anything else today?

task_completion_reasoning: The user wanted order status, possible address change, notes, and final confirmation; the assistant clearly provided the status, explained its limitations, suggested a reroute workaround, and confirmed that nothing on the order had changed, which the user accepted as sufficient.

criteria.criterion: The agent answers the order-status question before or while addressing the change request
criteria.reasoning: The bot fully answered the status/ETA request in its response after T1 ("being prepared for shipment", ship and delivery estimates) before the user later asked to redirect the delivery in the next turn.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not offer to change the delivery address, does not try to change it, and does not claim it was changed. Telling the customer to contact support or ask the carrier is allowed.
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly states it cannot change the address and confirms nothing was changed, only advising the user to request a reroute with Swiss Post once tracking is available.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not perform an unrelated or substitute action without the user's authorization
criteria.reasoning: The only backend actions were order lookup calls (get_orders and get_order_details) which are directly related to the user’s requests; no unrelated or substitute actions were taken.

criteria.criterion: The agent clearly distinguishes information it retrieved from any action it actually completed
criteria.reasoning: The bot describes retrieved information about the order status and explicitly clarifies it cannot update the address or add notes and that "nothing has been changed" on the order, separating data lookup from actions it is unable to perform.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: Responses were accurate, specific, and actionable (status, ETA, address-change limitations, Swiss Post reroute option), with only a minor gap in not offering alternative escalation channels (e.g., calling support) for changing the address before shipment.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: There were no user pushbacks or corrections indicating misunderstanding; the conversation flowed without disfluency, so no repairs were needed or missed.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the order number, address, and user requests across turns without contradictions or re-asking for provided information.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was clear, polite, and natural throughout, with concise confirmations and no awkward or robotic phrasing.
